name: Mupirocin
route_note: 2% ointment or cream applied to skin; 2% nasal ointment for staphylococcal decolonisation.

discovery.note: Pseudomonic acid A was isolated from Pseudomonas fluorescens; reported in Nature in 1971.

tagline: Topical antibiotic for impetigo and nasal MRSA decolonisation
summary: Mupirocin is a topical antibiotic derived from Pseudomonas fluorescens that inhibits bacterial isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase. It is used for impetigo and other superficial skin infections and as nasal ointment to clear Staphylococcus aureus, including MRSA, before surgery or in outbreaks.
mechanism: Mupirocin mimics isoleucyl-adenylate and binds bacterial isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase, preventing charging of tRNA with isoleucine; protein and RNA synthesis stop. It is bacteriostatic at low concentrations and bactericidal at those achieved topically.

It is rapidly hydrolysed to inactive monic acid in the body, so it is used only topically. Low-level resistance arises from ileS point mutations; high-level resistance is mediated by plasmid-borne mupA (ileS2) or mupB genes encoding an alternative synthetase.
uses: Impetigo caused by S. aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes
Nasal decolonisation of S. aureus/MRSA (e.g. before surgery, in outbreaks or dialysis patients)

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Beecham scientists report pseudomonic acid from Pseudomonas fluorescens.

history.title: UK launch
history.detail: Mupirocin ointment (Bactroban) is launched in the UK.

history.title: High-level resistance
history.detail: Plasmid-mediated high-level mupirocin resistance (mupA) is increasingly reported among staphylococci with widespread use.

history.title: Decolonisation trial
history.detail: An NEJM trial shows nasal mupirocin plus chlorhexidine bathing halves surgical-site S. aureus infections in carriers.

pk.metabolism: rapidly hydrolysed to inactive monic acid

common: Burning or stinging at application site
Rhinitis and headache with nasal use
serious: Polyethylene glycol absorption from ointment in extensive burns or renal impairment

facts: Mupirocin's isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase target is unique among clinically used antibiotics, so there is no cross-resistance with other classes.
